title: Extract Text That Survives
objective: After this lesson you will be able to extract page text with correct reading order via pdf.js, repair hyphenation and strip running furniture (headers/footers/page numbers), and normalize whitespace into clean paragraphs.
why: Raw extraction output is famously ugly: words split mid-syllable, 'Page 12 of 40' interleaved mid-sentence, two-column layouts interleaved line-by-line. Downstream stages (validation, chunking, retrieval) inherit every artifact — extraction quality is the ceiling on everything after it. An hour here saves ten in debugging retrieval misses later.

blocks.text: Reading order is not line order

PDF text items carry coordinates, not paragraphs — `getTextContent()` returns items in *paint order*, which for two-column layouts interleaves left and right columns line by line. Correct extraction sorts by geometry: group items into lines by vertical position, order lines top-to-bottom, and within multi-column pages split columns by horizontal gaps first. Libraries (pdf.js) expose coordinates; the ordering logic is yours.

blocks.caption: getTextContent gives positioned fragments — ordering is your code's job

blocks.text: Line-end splits ('cus-\ntomer') must rejoin; genuine compounds ('state-of-the-art') must survive. Rule: rejoin **letter-hyphen-newline-lowercase-letter** only — mid-line hyphens, spaced dashes, and hyphen-newline-capitalized continuations stay untouched. State the rule in a comment; cleanup without stated rules is unreviewable.

blocks.caption: One regex with a lowercase-continuation guard — verify on samples

blocks.text: Strip the furniture: headers, footers, page numbers

Running heads ('ACME Manual — Page 12 of 40') repeat every page and poison retrieval with identical chunks. Strip by repetition: lines identical (after trimming digits) across ≥3 pages are furniture until proven otherwise. Page numbers match `^\d+$` or `Page \d+` patterns positionally (top/bottom 10% of page). Never strip by content blacklist ('Chapter' might be furniture on page tops and real text in body — position + repetition decide).

blocks.caption: Repeated + marginal = furniture: the two-signal rule

blocks.text: Extraction yields chaotic spacing: multiple spaces, stray newlines mid-sentence, tabs-as-layout. Normalize in fixed order: (1) join soft line breaks *within* paragraphs (single newline → space) while keeping blank lines as paragraph breaks; (2) collapse horizontal runs to single spaces; (3) trim. Order matters — collapsing before joining destroys the paragraph signals you need.

blocks.title: Repair the damage
blocks.note: Run it: expect "The customer portal spans multiple lines.\n\nPage 12 of 40" — hyphen rejoined, soft break joined, spaces collapsed, and the blank-line paragraph break preserved (that preservation is the feature, not a bug). (Furniture stripping needs multi-page repetition — that's the stripFurniture function above, run it on your own pages.)

items: Order by geometry (columns, then lines top-to-bottom) — paint order lies on multi-column pages
Dehyphenate letter-hyphen-newline-lowercase only; real compounds survive by rule, stated in comments
Furniture = repeated + marginal (position), never content blacklists
Whitespace pipeline order: join soft breaks → collapse runs → trim; paragraph breaks are blank lines

exercise.prompt: Given three extracted pages where each contains the header 'ACME Manual' at top and footer 'Page N of 40' at bottom, plus body text with hyphen splits: (a) run the practice repair on one hyphenated body paragraph in the playground; (b) hand-simulate stripFurniture on the header/footer lines (show the digit-masked keys and counts); (c) state what breaks if you strip by the blacklist ['ACME', 'Page'] instead.
hints: Practice repair first on a body sample with a cus-\ntomer style split — confirm the rejoined output before touching furniture.
Masked keys: 'ACME Manual' → 'ACME Manual' (count 3), 'Page 12 of 40' → 'Page # of #' (count 3) — both repeated + marginal → stripped.

Blacklist breakage: a body sentence 'See Page 12 for details' or 'ACME announced…' matches the blacklist mid-page (not marginal, count 1) and gets wrongly deleted — position + repetition is the guard.
exercise.why: The exercise separates the three extraction repairs (order/hyphen/furniture/whitespace) and proves why the furniture rule needs both signals — repetition without position deletes legitimately repeated body phrases; position without repetition deletes unique marginalia like captions.

quiz.q: Two-column PDF extracts with sentences interleaved left-right-left-right. Cause + fix?
options: Paint order ≠ reading order: sort items geometrically (split columns by x-gaps, then lines top-to-bottom)
quiz.explain: Items carry coordinates, not reading sequence. Geometry-first ordering (columns, then lines) restores the author's order — extraction callers own this logic.

quiz.q: 'well-\nKnown' vs 'cus-\ntomer' — rejoin which, and by what rule?
options: Both — all hyphens at line ends are artifacts
Rejoin cus-tomer (lowercase continuation); preserve well-Known (capitalized continuation signals genuine compound/proper noun)
quiz.explain: Lowercase continuation marks line-break splits; capitals mark real compounds. The rule must be stated in comments — silent joining corrupts compounds.

quiz.q: Why not strip headers via a content blacklist like ['ACME', 'Page']?
options: Body text legitimately contains those words mid-page — stripping needs repetition + marginal position, not content matching
quiz.explain: 'See Page 12 for details' is body, not furniture. Two-signal rule (repeated across pages AND marginal position) distinguishes them; content matching cannot.

summary: Extract with geometry (columns, lines, order), dehyphenate by rule, strip furniture by repetition + position, normalize whitespace in pipeline order. Extraction quality ceilings everything downstream.
